facts.statement: Herugavialis is an extinct marine gavialoid crocodilian from the Eocene (Lutetian) Mokattam Formation of Egypt.
facts.quote: Herugavialis ("Horus gharial") is an extinct genus of marine gavialoid crocodilian known from the Eocene (Lutetian stage) Mokattam Formation of Egypt.

facts.statement: Herugavialis lacked a maxilla process within its lacrimal gland, a feature present in all living crocodilians.
facts.quote: Herugavialis did not have a maxilla process within its lacrimal gland, whereas all extant (living) crocodilians do.

facts.statement: In 2026 the species was reassigned to the new genus Herugavialis by Burke and colleagues.
facts.quote: In a 2026 study, it was moved to its own genus, Herugavialis.

facts.statement: The genus name references the Egyptian god Horus and the Great Sphinx’s missing nose, alluding to the missing premaxilla of the holotype skull.
facts.quote: This genus name references the Ancient Egyptian god Horus, widely thought to be depicted in the Great Sphinx (built from the same geological formation that Herugavialis was identified from), as well as the Sphinx's lack of a nose, referencing the missing nasal region (premaxilla) of the holotype skull of Herugavialis.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Herugavialis within Gavialidae, more closely related to the gharial than to the false gharial.
facts.quote: Herugavialis was recovered more closely related to the gharial than the false gharial, within Gavialidae.

facts.statement: The type locality for Herugavialis is the Mokattam Formation in Egypt.
The table lists the age of Herugavialis as Middle Miocene.
CT scans revealed telescoped orbits as a diagnostic feature of Herugavialis cairensis.
The authors hypothesize that warming in the Miocene allowed a rebound of gavialoid diversity before their eventual extinction in the Late Miocene, possibly caused by the Messinian Salinity Crisis.
